introduction.situation: Religion and theology study how people understand the ultimate and the human condition and how that understanding is carried in texts, practices and communities.
introduction.complication: The existing groups mix library classes, research codes and duplicated topics, so the real objects of study are hidden.
introduction.question: How is everything in religion and theology divided?
introduction.answer: Religion and theology are divided by what the inquiry is about: the ultimate and the human condition, authoritative text, practice, and community and institution, moving from the referent to its carriers.

governing_thought: Religion and theology are divided by what the inquiry is about: the ultimate and the human condition, authoritative text, practice, and community and institution, moving from the referent to its carriers.

key_line.rank_note: The pillars run from the referent of religion to the texts, practices and communities that carry it.

points.statement: The ultimate and the human condition is what religious thought is about, including its doctrines, its philosophy and the particular religions that hold beliefs about it.
points.name: The ultimate and the human condition is what religious thought is about, including its doctrines, its philosophy and the particular religions that hold beliefs about it.

support.rank_note: General inquiry comes before the particular traditions it is applied to.

points.statement: General inquiry into religion examines belief, myth, doctrine and the philosophy of the ultimate across traditions.
points.name: General inquiry into religion examines belief, myth, doctrine and the philosophy of the ultimate across traditions.

support.rank_note: From the broad study of religions to doctrine and philosophy.

points.statement: Particular religious traditions each hold a distinct understanding of the ultimate and the human condition.
points.name: Particular religious traditions each hold a distinct understanding of the ultimate and the human condition.

support.rank_note: The Abrahamic traditions come first, then Buddhism, eastern and other traditions.

points.statement: The Abrahamic traditions of Christianity, Judaism and Islam understand the ultimate through a single God and a shared lineage of revelation.
points.name: The Abrahamic traditions of Christianity, Judaism and Islam understand the ultimate through a single God and a shared lineage of revelation.

support.rank_note: Ordered from Christianity to Judaism to Islam, following the original grouping.

points.statement: Buddhism, the eastern traditions and other religious traditions understand the ultimate and the human condition outside the Abrahamic lineage.
points.name: Buddhism, the eastern traditions and other religious traditions understand the ultimate and the human condition outside the Abrahamic lineage.

support.rank_note: From Buddhism to the wider eastern traditions and then to other traditions.

points.statement: Studies in religious traditions (excl. Eastern, Jewish, Christian and Islamic traditions)
points.name: Studies in religious traditions (excl. Eastern, Jewish, Christian and Islamic traditions)

points.statement: World religions are the major living traditions, each with its own account of the ultimate.

points.statement: Authoritative text is what scripture and religious law are about, since both are bodies of writing that carry binding religious authority.
points.name: Authoritative text is what scripture and religious law are about, since both are bodies of writing that carry binding religious authority.

support.rank_note: Scripture comes before the law derived from it, from general to tradition-specific law.

points.name: Religious law in general. Comparative religious law. Jurisprudence

points.statement: Practice is what ministry, worship and the lived expression of religion in society and culture are about.
points.name: Practice is what ministry, worship and the lived expression of religion in society and culture are about.

support.rank_note: From the practical work of ministry to religion as lived in wider culture.

points.statement: Worship and ritual are the acts through which believers express and enact their faith together.
points.name: Worship and ritual are the acts through which believers express and enact their faith together.

points.statement: Community and institution is what denominations and the church's own governing law are about, as the organised bodies that carry religion.
